https://www.itv.com/news/calendar/2025-0.title: Fire service 'fell short' after Storm Babet flood victim found by son, inquest told
https://www.itv.com/news/calendar/2025-0.text:
A fire brigade has admitted it "fell short" after the body of an 83-year-old woman was found in floodwater by her son following aborted attempts to rescue her.
Paul Gilbert discovered his mother, Maureen, floating in the water at her home in Tapton Terrace, Chesterfield, Derbyshire, on 21 October 2023.
Mrs Gilbert had become trapped when the River Rother burst its banks and flooded her house during Storm Babet.
Chesterfield Coroner’s Court was told firefighters did everything they could to rescue Mrs Gilbert at her terraced property on the evening of 20 October, but were unable to reach her.
Crews failed to return to the property after a request to go back was “mislogged” while Derbyshire Fire and Rescue Service’s control room systems were down.
Mrs Gilbert was one of at least seven people who died as a result of Storm Babet, which caused disruption across the UK.
Neil Porteous, an incident commander for the fire service, said he requested that Tapton Terrace be reinspected the  following day but this “was not communicated”, the inquest heard.
Clive Stanbrook, an area manager for the service, told the inquest on Tuesday: “This had clearly not been handed over to the next shift the next day. We should have gone back in the morning. We fell short.”
Parts of the control room system had “completely failed” when the request to check on Mrs Gilbert was made, the inquest heard.
The coroner was told wheelie bins and fence panels were floating in the water when firefighters attempted to make contact with Mrs Gilbert the evening before.
Mr Porteous said: “It was massive amounts of water. The front gardens were completely underwater. It was a difficult scene to look at.
“Numerous wheelie bins just floating on top of the water. Loads of debris floating. Manhole covers had lifted as well.”
Mr Porteous said the crew knew Mrs Gilbert was inside the property because her son had spoken to her on the phone but then lost contact.
He said: “It was just a very, very difficult scene. We had done everything we could possibly do.
“We don’t like to leave people behind. It was just too dangerous – it was getting too dark.
“The crew said ‘Can we go in?’ and at that point I had to stop them and explain why, and they understood.”
At 7.22pm, the rescue crew left the scene at Tapton Terrace and Mr Porteous made the request for a reinspection the next day.
Mr Gilbert said it was “disappointing” that he discovered his mother himself.
The inquest will continue on Wednesday morning.

https://www.itv.com/news/central/2025-09.title: Street where 83-year-old woman died in Storm Babet floods 'still poses a risk to residents'
https://www.itv.com/news/central/2025-09.text:
An inquest into the death of an 83-year old woman from Derbyshire who died in Storm Babet has found that the road where she lived still poses a risk to residents.
The coroner gave a narrative verdict and said he will issue a prevention of future deaths report to highlight the continued risk of flooding.
Maureen Gilbert, was found dead on October 21 2023 after her home in Tapton Terrace in Chesterfield was flooded during the storm.
She was found by her son Paul Gilbert after the nearby River Rother burst its banks.

He said after the inquest: "More money needs to be available and more long-term plans need to be put in, I still believe that dredging rivers and cleaning rivers out for me is the most important thing, building rivers it helps but the water has got to go somewhere eventually.
"She was one of at least seven people who died as a result of Storm Babet, which caused disruption across the UK."
The future deaths report will be issued to the relevant government minister, the Environment Agency and Derbyshire County Council.
The coroner Matthew Kewley said he placed no blame on Derbyshire Fire and Rescue Service (DFRS) for its actions at Tapton Terrace, against the backdrop of the brigade fielding about 1,600 emergency calls across two days, and its control room dealing with two separate systems failures.
But he said he intended to issue a prevention of future deaths report, external highlighting the risk to residents on Tapton Terrace, to the relevant government minister, the Environment Agency, and Derbyshire County Council.
He said: "We have heard evidence of ongoing discussions of what might happen and could happen, and this will come down to funding, which is no business of mine.
"But it doesn't take away from my concern that Tapton Terrace is in the same position it was in 2007 and again in 2023, and someone has now lost their life."
Maureen's neighbours previously described how five feet of water engulfed the inside of their properties “within minutes” of the River Rother bursting its banks.
Around 400 homes in the Chesterfield area were evacuated during the storm.
"We have made changes"
Neil Longden, who was the Environment Agency’s operations manager for Yorkshire, gave evidence to the inquest, and was asked why there were no flood defences near Tapton Terrace, which is next to the River Rother.
Deputy Chief Fire Officer Clive Stanbrook said after the hearing: "I want to give assurances that we have already learned from this incident; we have invested heavily in our systems and we have made changes to our operational processes, something noted by the coroner.
"The coroner was in no doubt that the firefighters who attended did all that they reasonably and safely could to save Maureen's life, and he went on to say that he was satisfied that the outcome would not have been different had the re-inspection taken place."

Derbyshire Police referred itself to the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) after Mrs Gilbert's death.
The force said the referral was mandatory due to officers being involved with the evacuation of homes in the area.
The government has previously said the Environment Agency was working to "fully review what happened".
